title: Bar Kokhba (132–135 CE)
hookLine: a second revolt is crushed, and Jews are barred from Jerusalem

cards: "There shall step forth a star out of Jacob." That's a line from the book of Numbers, spoken by Balaam, a promise of a ruler rising from Israel.
Years after the Temple burned, a new Jewish commander rose up against Rome, and Rabbi Akiva, a teacher honored by the sages, looked at him and reached for that verse.
His name was Koziba, and Akiva read it into the verse: not a star, but Koziba, steps forth out of Jacob. When he saw the man, Akiva said: this is the king, the anointed one.
The fighter became known as Bar Kokhba, son of a star.

teach.h: GRASS WILL GROW FROM YOUR CHEEKS.
teach.b: The story is told in the Jerusalem Talmud, in tractate Taanit. Not everyone agreed with Akiva.
Another sage, Rabbi Yochanan ben Torta, answered with a sharp, sad line, in paraphrase: Akiva, grass will grow out of your cheeks, and the son of David still won't have come.
You'll be long buried before the redemption arrives, and this isn't it. The revolt was crushed.

teach.h: BETAR FALLS ON THE NINTH OF AV.
teach.b: The Mishnah, in the same list of grief we met with the Temple's fall, records that on the ninth of Av the fortress of Betar was captured.

teach.h: SON OF A STAR, SON OF A LIE.
teach.b: Rome made Jerusalem a Roman city with a new name, Aelia Capitolina, and Jews were barred from entering it.
Other rabbinic passages call the commander Bar Koziba, and some readers hear in it son of a lie, a bitter play on the same name. One man, two nicknames, and the gap between them is the story.
The rabbis didn't hide that their honored teacher backed a hope that failed.

They kept Akiva's words and Yochanan ben Torta's answer side by side, the way they kept Hillel and Shammai, and the page leaves a question for whoever reads it: what do you do with a hope that failed?

how: The fall of Betar is remembered on Tisha B'Av, the ninth of Av, alongside the destruction of both Temples, in the fast and the readings of the day.

o: son of a star, the name for a failed revolt's leader
son of David, the king the prophets promised
son of Jacob, a title for any of Israel's tribes

games.q: the second revolt — tap the pairs.
p: grass will grow from your cheeks
the fortress that fell on the ninth of Av

s: every sage agreed Bar Kokhba was the promised king

the rabbis hid that Akiva backed the revolt
they kept his words and the answer to him side by side.
later rabbinic writing also calls him Bar Koziba
a bitter play on his name: son of a lie, beside son of a star.

games.q: you're a sage in the study hall. Rabbi Akiva, an honored teacher, says this commander is the promised king. what do you say?
o: tell him plainly that he's wrong.
games.why: Rabbi Yochanan ben Torta tells him: grass will grow from your cheeks and the son of David still won't have come. the Talmud keeps both their words.

practice: Let one hope come back to you that didn't come true: a plan, a person you trusted, a cause you were sure of.

Say plainly, inside, this didn't work, with no reason and no lesson yet, and notice that you are still here, still breathing, after it. As the week closes, look back too: a wall, two schools, a fall, a fortress, a coffin, a table.
If you pray, you can bring the hope that failed to God.

wordCard.voice: Bar Kokhba. Son of a star, Akiva called him; the revolt was crushed, Betar fell, and Jews were barred from Jerusalem. The rabbis kept the hope and the failure on the record.

orig.note: Hebrew: star, the word in "a star out of Jacob" that Akiva read as the commander's name.

carryVoice: Your line: after the revolt. Akiva's words are still there, and so is the answer that told him he was wrong. Day nine hundred three, and a week complete.
